correctness.rationale: Theorem 5 and Theorem 6 of arXiv:2309.04012v1 give the two exact Fibonacci run-length formulas. The weighted binary-word prefix decomposition yields H(z)=A(z)/(1-zA(z)); the five weight series have rational denominators verified directly by the Fibonacci recurrence. Independent digit-parity enumeration agrees on the first 1200 indices and all five full dyadic moment series through length fourteen. Fibonacci addition identities establish coordinate monotonicity, an induction proves positive association, and a strict conditional covariance occurs whenever the binary length is at least two. The three cubic characteristic polynomials have three disjoint rational root intervals each, proving dominance. Rational bounds prove the mixed spectral root exceeds the mean-product scale but lies below the geometric mean of the two square-moment roots. Residue coefficients are nonzero and positive, implying the exact exponential Pearson decay. Finite tests are support, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The closely relevant 2023 primary paper explicitly proves the two marginal run-length representations and marginal means, but its inspected Theorems 4-6 and Section 6 do not give the mixed dyadic moment or positive-but-asymptotically-zero correlation. OEIS A030186 already records the squared marginal recurrence, which is deliberately not asserted as novel. The 2018 Zhang-Grossman paper gives formulas for powers of recurrence sequences, not dyadic binomial-sum dependence. Search of published mathematical findings and sequence/database aliases did not locate a dominating explicit comparison. An implicit equivalent in a general tensor-matrix framework remains a non-negligible risk, not a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: General tensor products of the published 2-regular representations might have an unindexed explicit formula equivalent to the new joint moment.
The closest fourth-order binomial-transform publication was not inspectable in full, though its announced objects differ.

value.rationale: The two specific binomial-parity counts are published natural companion transforms with known separate means. Their dependence is therefore a motivated invariant, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The new theorem proves that their covariance is strictly positive at every nondegenerate dyadic length while Pearson correlation nevertheless decreases exponentially, and identifies its exact algebraic decay rate from three spectral roots. This sharp finite-to-asymptotic contrast adds structural information not given by the marginal means or a table of one squared-moment sequence.
